game-ad-path.intro: BloodHound output is on the table. Find the path.

challenges.q: You have a domain user. Kerberoastable service account runs as a service with local admin on a server. Order the chain.
items: Request a service ticket for the SPN as any domain user
Crack the ticket offline to recover the service account password
Use the account to access the server where it is local admin
Enumerate sessions to find a domain admin and harvest a ticket
challenges.why: Kerberoast, crack, use local admin, then hunt for higher-value sessions.

challenges.q: The service account has unconstrained delegation and a domain admin occasionally authenticates to it. Order the exploitation.
items: Compromise the delegation-enabled host
Wait for or force a privileged authentication to it
Extract the cached ticket-granting ticket from memory
Use the ticket to impersonate the domain admin
challenges.why: Unconstrained delegation caches tickets for anyone who authenticates, which is the whole attack.

challenges.q: You find GenericAll on a user object and GenericWrite on a group. Which step reaches privilege?
items: Set a Service Principal Name on the user then Kerberoast and crack it, or add yourself to the group
Delete the group
Rename the user
Reset the computer account
challenges.why: Targeted Kerberoasting via SPN write, or direct group membership, both escalate.

challenges.q: Which account hash is required for a golden ticket?
items: Any domain admin
The krbtgt account hash
A service account hash
The domain SID only
challenges.why: krbtgt signs ticket-granting tickets, so its key forges tickets for anything.

challenges.q: Order the steps of a DCSync attack.
items: Obtain an account with directory replication rights
Impersonate a domain controller to the target DC
Request replication of account secrets
Recover the krbtgt hash and forge tickets
challenges.why: Replication rights then the replication protocol yields hashes without touching the DC directly.

challenges.q: What is the single most effective structural defence in AD?
items: Tiered administration with separate privileged accounts and restricted logon rights
Longer passwords
More domain controllers
Disabling Kerberos
challenges.why: Tiering prevents the credential reuse that makes most AD chains work.

game-kerberos-flow.intro: Assemble the ticket exchange and name the abuse.

challenges.q: Order a normal Kerberos authentication for a file share.
items: Client authenticates to the KDC and receives a TGT
Client requests a service ticket for the file server SPN
KDC returns a service ticket encrypted with the service account key
Client presents the service ticket to the file server
challenges.why: TGT first, then service tickets per resource, presented to the resource.

challenges.q: What exactly is cracked in Kerberoasting?
items: The TGT
The service ticket, which is encrypted with the service account password key
The session key
The domain SID
challenges.why: The service ticket is encrypted with a key derived from the service account password, so it is an offline crack target.

challenges.q: What must be true for ASREP roasting to work?
items: Kerberos must be disabled
The account must have pre-authentication disabled
The password must be strong
SMB signing must be off
challenges.why: Without pre-auth, the KDC returns a crackable response to anyone who asks.

challenges.q: Order an attack using resource-based constrained delegation.
items: Find an object you can write msDS-AllowedToActOnBehalfOfOtherIdentity on
Place a computer account you control in that attribute
Use S4U2Self and S4U2Proxy to obtain a service ticket as a privileged user
Access the target service as that user
challenges.why: Writing the delegation attribute grants your controlled principal the right to impersonate.

challenges.q: Why does disabling pre-auth only on one account create risk?
items: It slows the KDC
That account becomes remotely roastable with no credentials required
It breaks DNS
It needs a reboot
challenges.why: Anyone who can reach the KDC can request a crackable response for that account.

challenges.q: A silver ticket forges a service ticket. What is required?
items: The krbtgt hash
The target service account hash and its SID
The domain admin password
Physical access
challenges.why: Service tickets are signed with the service account key, so that key alone forges them for that service.
